q-213133.name: Question 1
q-213133.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $2x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,15)?$
q-213133.worked_solution:
The scalar multiplication properties of congruences state that for $k\in Z,$ we have the following:

- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)\,⟹\,ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,n)$

- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)\,⟹\,ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,kn)$

The modulus equals $15$ in all statements, which suggests we'll need to use the first property.

Notice that the coefficient of $x$ is $2,$ and $8\cdot 2=16$ is one larger than the modulus. Therefore, we can reduce the coefficient of $x$ to unity as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ≡1\, & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ 8\cdot 2x & ≡8\cdot 1\, & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ 16x & ≡8\, & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ x+15x & ≡8\, & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ x+0x & ≡8\, & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ x & ≡8\, & (\text{mod}\,15)\end{aligned}
$$

x≡5(mod14)

x≡1(mod14)

Correct

The scalar multiplication properties of congruences state that for k∈Z, we have the following:

  • a≡b(modn)⟹ka≡kb(modn)

  • a≡b(modn)⟹ka≡kb(modkn)

The modulus equals 14 in all statements, which suggests we'll need to use the first property.

Notice that the coefficient of x is 3, and 5⋅3=15 is one larger than the modulus. Therefore, we can reduce the coefficient of x to unity as follows:

3x≡1(mod14)5⋅3x≡5⋅1(mod14)15x≡5(mod14)x+14x≡5(mod14)x+0x≡5(mod14)x≡5(mod14)
